PAPERS.title: Exposure to wildfire smoke and risk of mortality and hospitalization among hemodialysis patients in the Western United States: Effect modification by extreme heat events.
PAPERS.short: Song Fresenius hemodialysis ESKD wildfire smoke plume PM2.5 extreme heat case-crossover mortality West US 2010-2018
PAPERS.pm: Smoke-plume presence (satellite plume polygons) and wildfire-attributed PM2.5 at each dialysis facility; extreme heat events
PAPERS.endpoint: All-cause mortality and hospitalization, lag 0
PAPERS.affil: University of Maryland School of Public Health, USA; University of Maryland School of Public Health, USA
PAPERS.n: 55,223 adult hemodialysis patients at Fresenius clinics in California, Oregon and Washington, warm seasons 2010-2018; conditional quasi-Poisson. A smoke plume overhead raised same-day mortality (RR 1.19, 1.11-1.27); each 10 ug/m3 of wildfire PM2.5 raised mortality 3% (RR 1.03, 1.02-1.06) and hospitalization 1% (1.01, 1.00-1.03). Plume plus extreme heat gave RR 1.92 (1.71-2.17) against 1.02 (0.95-1.10) for plume alone, so the plume signal is mostly heat-coincident. Exposure is assigned to the clinic, not the residence, and wildfire PM2.5 is a modelled split of total PM2.5; the interaction contrast is large enough that residual confounding by heat timing remains the main threat. Relevance: a dialysis population attends clinics thrice weekly, which makes clinic-sited low-cost monitors a cheap, exact exposure point.

PAPERS.title: Long-Term Exposure to PM2.5 Components and Respiratory Disease Mortality in South China: The Pearl River Cohort Study
PAPERS.short: Huang Wei Pearl River Cohort PM2.5 components NH4 NO3 BC OM SO4 Cl respiratory mortality quantile g-computation South China
PAPERS.pm: Long-term PM2.5 components (NH4+, NO3-, BC, OM, SO4 2-, Cl-), modelled surfaces
PAPERS.endpoint: Respiratory disease mortality
PAPERS.affil: Sun Yat-sen University, China; Sun Yat-sen University, China
PAPERS.n: 182,009 Pearl River Cohort participants; marginal structural Cox models for single components and quantile g-computation for the mixture. All six components raised respiratory mortality, single-component HRs 1.42-2.75 (increments not given in the abstract). Each quartile increase in the mixture index gave HR 1.29 (1.23-1.34), with nitrate carrying the largest weight (0.48), then organic matter and chloride. Older adults, non-smokers and non-exercisers were most susceptible (HRs 1.25-2.02). Component surfaces are model products whose errors are correlated across species, so the weight ranking partly reflects which component the model resolves best; HRs of 1.4-2.8 per component are implausibly large without the increment. Relevance: nitrate is the semi-volatile, hygroscopic fraction behind most low-cost-versus-reference disagreement in humid seasons.

PAPERS.title: Independent evaluation of Aurora air pollution forecasts beyond benchmark skill
PAPERS.short: Parthenope independent evaluation Aurora 0.4 degree air pollution foundation model CAMS persistence stations negative PM2.5 2024
PAPERS.pm: Forecast PM2.5 and PM10 (Aurora foundation model, 0.4 degree) against CAMS and hourly background stations
PAPERS.endpoint: MSE skill vs persistence, station MAE, physical consistency, input sensitivity
PAPERS.affil: Parthenope University of Naples, Italy; Parthenope University of Naples, Italy
PAPERS.n: Preprint. 96 initialisations across 2024 of the released Aurora air-pollution checkpoint, scored against CAMS, persistence and hourly background stations in three regions. Relative to persistence, Aurora cut MSE by 38.1-42.6% for PM2.5 and 49.1-52.3% for PM10, and its station MAE beat the benchmark-selected CAMS fields in all six region-pollutant pairs with bootstrap intervals excluding zero. But at +12 h, 6.27% of PM2.5 and 7.84% of PM10 grid values were negative, the model gives no forecast distribution, and its response to perturbed emission inputs is untested against real emission change. Background stations only, so urban hotspots are unscored. Relevance: dense low-cost networks are the obvious test bed for exactly the near-source skill this evaluation could not reach.

PAPERS.title: Forecasting hourly size-resolved ambient ultrafine particles with size-specific historical windows.
PAPERS.short: Shenzhen Mini-WRAS size-resolved ultrafine particle hourly forecasting MLR RF XGBoost LSTM history window 2023-2025
PAPERS.pm: Ultrafine particle number in eight bins 10-100 nm, Mini-WRAS, one urban site
PAPERS.endpoint: One-hour-ahead NRMSE by size bin and history window
PAPERS.affil: Sun Yat-sen University, China; Sun Yat-sen University, China
PAPERS.n: 8,982 quality-controlled hourly observations (Sep 2023-Jun 2025) from a Mini-WRAS at an urban Shenzhen site; 270 model-window-target configurations (MLR, RF, XGBoost, LSTM, BiLSTM; 1-24 h histories) scored on the same 533 test hours. Best NRMSE was 60.2% at 10 nm and 22.1% at 14 nm against 13.4-14.8% at 19-100 nm; a 2 h history was best for 10-19 nm and 4 h for 27-100 nm, while the summed UFP target reached 13.7% at 12 h. Several model classes tied, so architecture mattered less than window. One site, one-step-ahead, and no meteorological or traffic covariates are described. Relevance: aggregate number forecasts hide the poorly predictable nucleation mode, which is also the size range low-cost counters miss.

PAPERS.title: DnNP: Denoising Input Uncertainty in Neural Processes
PAPERS.short: Tohidian Elia denoising neural processes input uncertainty PM2.5 spatial interpolation air quality sensors 2026
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 from real-world air-quality sensor networks used as a spatial-interpolation benchmark
PAPERS.endpoint: Interpolation RMSE and negative log-likelihood
PAPERS.n: Preprint. Denoising Neural Processes extend the neural-process meta-learner to treat inputs as noisy, trained by variational inference, with a proof that the Bayes-optimal predictor under input noise lies in the model class and that fixed-variance plug-in models carry an irreducible KL gap. On PM2.5 spatial interpolation from real-world air-quality sensors the method cut RMSE by up to 30% and NLL by up to 73% against standard neural processes. The abstract names neither the network, its sensor type nor the baseline beyond vanilla NPs, so 'real-world sensors' cannot be placed against kriging or calibrated-network practice. Relevance: modelling noisy and mis-located sensor inputs explicitly is exactly the low-cost network problem; worth reading if the PM data are PurpleAir-class.

PAPERS.title: Forecasting of aerosol optical depth over arid and semi-arid regions using time series and machine learning models.
PAPERS.short: Punjab ARIMA LSTM NARX forecasting Deep Blue AOD550 Thar Thal Karakum Kutch Kyzylkum Arabian deserts 2000-2030
PAPERS.pm: Monthly satellite AOD550 (MODIS Deep Blue), six Asian deserts
PAPERS.endpoint: Test RMSE and R2; 6-year AOD projection
PAPERS.affil: Swami Premanand Mahavidyalaya, India; Guru Nanak Dev University College, India
PAPERS.n: 294 monthly Deep Blue AOD550 values (Feb 2000-Jul 2024) for the Thar, Thal, Karakum, Kutch, Kyzylkum and Arabian deserts; ARIMA, LSTM and NARX evaluated on a 44-month test set. NARX was best (test RMSE 0.0180-0.0275) over LSTM (0.0215-0.0350, R2 0.53-0.70) and ARIMA (0.0250-0.0400, R2 0.40-0.60), and was used to project AOD to July 2030. Monthly means of a column optical quantity carry no surface PM information, and a six-year recursive forecast from 250 training points has no credible uncertainty statement. Relevance: marginal - desert dust is the regime where AOD-to-PM2.5 conversion and optical low-cost sensors both fail, but this paper does not touch the surface.

PAPERS.title: Numerical Analysis of an Early-Arriving East Asian Dust Storm in 2026: Evaluation, Size-Resolved Dust Contribution, and Source Attribution
PAPERS.short: Anhui WRF-Chem GOCART Shao KOK dust schemes February 2026 East Asian dust storm size-resolved PM10 Gobi source attribution
PAPERS.pm: Size-resolved mineral dust contribution to surface PM10 and AOD, WRF-Chem with three emission schemes
PAPERS.endpoint: AOD skill (R, RMSE), dust mass by size bin, source attribution
PAPERS.affil: Anhui & Huaihe River Institute of Hydraulic Research, China; Anhui Institute of Meteorological Sciences, China
PAPERS.n: WRF-Chem case study of the 18-23 February 2026 dust storm that reached the Yangtze basin, comparing GOCART, Shao2001 and KOK emission schemes. A tuned GOCART run matched observed AOD best (R 0.74, RMSE 0.16). Size bins 5-8 supplied over 90% of dust mass in surface PM10; regional emission peaked above 4.0 Tg on 20 February while area-mean loading peaked at about 90 mg/m2 a day later; the Gobi supplied about two-thirds of the loading. Validation is against AOD, not surface PM10 monitors, and one event cannot rank schemes. Relevance: coarse-dominated dust episodes are where PM2.5-tuned optical sensors under-read PM10 most; event-specific size splits like this are what a dust correction needs.

PAPERS.title: Long-term nitrous acid evolution modulates ozone and secondary aerosol variations in global megacities.
PAPERS.short: Zhang Peking deep neural network global surface HONO reconstruction 2005-2021 megacities ozone particulate nitrate drivers
PAPERS.pm: Secondary PM2.5 (particulate nitrate) and ozone driven by reconstructed surface HONO
PAPERS.endpoint: HONO trends and attributed O3 / nitrate change
PAPERS.affil: Peking University, China; Peking University, China
PAPERS.n: A deep neural network trained on worldwide field campaigns reconstructs surface HONO; Beijing fell 47.4% (2013-2021), Delhi rose 10.0% (2005-2018), and London, New York and Los Angeles declined slightly. HONO change is identified as a major driver of ozone and particulate nitrate variation, outweighing NOx and VOC abatement in Beijing and Delhi, and the framework recommends NOx control in summer and joint NOx, PM2.5 and direct-combustion cuts in winter. HONO is sparsely measured and campaign-biased, so the reconstruction and the attribution share one learned model; no uncertainty on the nitrate share is given in the abstract. Relevance: indirect - explains nitrate-driven PM2.5 trends that sensor networks record but cannot apportion.

PAPERS.title: Various ambient air pollutants, residential greenness, and risk of substance use disorders: a population-based cohort study.
PAPERS.short: Liu Xi'an UK Biobank PM2.5 PM10 PMcoarse NO2 NOx greenness incident substance use disorder Cox 10.9 y
PAPERS.pm: Residential PM2.5, PM2.5-10, PM10, NO2, NOx from land-use regression; 300 m greenness
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident substance use disorder
PAPERS.affil: Xi'an Jiaotong University, China; Xi'an Jiaotong University, China
PAPERS.n: 247,138 UK Biobank participants free of substance use disorder at baseline; 4,982 incident cases over a median 10.9 years. All five pollutants were positively associated; PM2.5 strongest (HR 1.111, 1.081-1.142), then PM10 (1.070, 1.054-1.086); the increment is not stated in the abstract, so the size of these HRs cannot be interpreted. Green space (HR 0.997, 0.996-0.998) was inversely associated and domestic garden attenuated the pollutant HRs in the high-exposure group. Effects were largest in older men and ever-smokers, the strata where residual confounding by deprivation and smoking intensity is worst; baseline LUR surfaces stand in for decade-long exposure. Relevance: low - an LUR cohort result without an increment adds a hazard ratio that cannot be pooled.

PAPERS.title: Particulate Matter is Not Associated With Disease Worsening in Patients With Multiple Sclerosis: Retrospective Results From a Clinic-Based Cohort in the Northeastern United States.
PAPERS.short: Lebiedz Chitnis Brigham MS Center PM2.5 satellite zip-code PIRA EDSS 6 Cox null northeastern US 2017-2023
PAPERS.pm: Monthly zip-code PM2.5 from an open satellite-derived dataset, baseline and time-varying annual means
PAPERS.endpoint: Time to progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA); time to EDSS >= 6
PAPERS.affil: Brigham and Women's Hospital, USA; University of Washington, USA
PAPERS.n: 3,040 people with MS at the Brigham MS Center, mean age 49.5, median EDSS 2.7, mean baseline PM2.5 5.8 ug/m3. Adjusted HRs were null for PIRA (baseline 1.01, 0.96-1.06; time-varying 0.98, 0.93-1.04) and for EDSS >= 6 (baseline 1.03, 0.94-1.13; time-varying 1.01, 0.92-1.10). The increment behind the HRs is not stated. Exposure contrast is narrow at New England levels, zip-code assignment blurs it further, and clinic-based retrospective ascertainment of PIRA is noisy, so the null mainly bounds large effects at low concentrations. Relevance: a well-powered null at ~6 ug/m3; resolving within-zip contrast would need denser measurement than satellite surfaces give.

PAPERS.title: Component-Specific PM2.5 Exposure and Arthritis Risk in China: Evidence of Differential Susceptibility in a National Cohort
PAPERS.short: Yan Li Sun Yat-sen national cohort PM2.5 components OM BC SO4 NO3 NH4 arthritis quantile g-computation middle-aged older China
PAPERS.pm: Short- and long-term PM2.5 mass and components (OM, BC, SO4 2-, NO3-, NH4+), modelled surfaces
PAPERS.endpoint: Arthritis prevalence
PAPERS.affil: Sun Yat-sen University, China; Sun Yat-sen University, China
PAPERS.n: 14,935 middle-aged and older adults in a nationally representative Chinese cohort; mixed-effects logistic regression and quantile g-computation. Both short- and long-term PM2.5 mass and organic matter, black carbon, sulfate and ammonium were reported to raise arthritis risk, with men and overweight or obese participants most vulnerable. The abstract gives no effect size, CI or increment, and does not say how arthritis was ascertained, so neither magnitude nor outcome specificity can be judged from the record. Component surfaces are correlated model products. Relevance: low until numbers appear; another component study where nitrate does not lead, unlike the Pearl River respiratory result today.

PAPERS.title: Ambient nitrogen dioxide and composition-specific risk of urolithiasis: a multicenter time-stratified case-crossover study.
PAPERS.short: Guangzhou Tianjin Guizhou urolithiasis stone composition NO2 PM10 inverse U-shaped case-crossover 128000 stones
PAPERS.pm: Six criteria pollutants incl. PM2.5 and PM10 (fixed-site monitors) with meteorology
PAPERS.endpoint: Laboratory-confirmed urinary stones by composition
PAPERS.affil: First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University, China; First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: 25,374 analysed urinary stones in Guangzhou with validation in Tianjin (99,552) and Guizhou (3,021); conditional logistic regression and GAMs over lags 0-7 and 6- to 12-month averages. The robust signal is NO2, strongest at lags 0 and 2-4 for carbonate apatite and calcium oxalate. PM10 showed mainly inverse or U-shaped associations with overall and composition-specific risk, and a PM10-carbonate apatite pattern was confirmed in Guizhou; no PM effect sizes are given in the abstract. Stones are dated at analysis, not symptom onset, so short lags are misaligned with formation. Relevance: low - a PM null-to-inverse result in a gas-driven outcome, carried for completeness.

PAPERS.title: High-Resolution PM2.5 Mortality Projections With Machine Learning Reveal Global Inequities Under Future Climate and Socioeconomic Pathways
PAPERS.short: CUHK CESM XGBoost 0.1 degree PM2.5 mortality GEMM SSP1 SSP2 SSP3 SSP5 2010 2050 emissions climate land use
PAPERS.pm: Annual PM2.5 from CESM bias-corrected and downscaled to 0.1 degree by XGBoost
PAPERS.endpoint: PM2.5-attributable deaths by age and cause, 2010 and 2050
PAPERS.affil: Chinese University of Hong Kong, China; Chinese University of Hong Kong, China
PAPERS.n: CESM factorial runs separating emissions, climate and land-use change, bias-corrected and refined to 0.1 degree with XGBoost, fed to GEMM. Present-day burden about 6.13 million deaths in 2010 (UI 5.77-6.48); by 2050 SSP1 removes about 1.1 million deaths and SSP3 adds about 0.5 million. Emissions dominate, climate change offsets part of the emission benefit, and the burden concentrates in people over 60 and in LMICs. The uncertainty interval covers the concentration-response function only; the ML downscaler is trained against present-day observations and is applied to 2050 states it has never seen. Relevance: the downscaler's skill rests on ground data that are thinnest in the LMICs that carry the burden.

PAPERS.title: Inequalities in greenspace access and their associations with all-cause and cause-specific mortality attributable to PM2.5: a global analysis from 2000 to 2020.
PAPERS.short: Shandong GBD 2021 PM2.5 attributable ASMR greenspace access Gini 204 countries 2000-2020 EAPC
PAPERS.pm: GBD 2021 ambient PM2.5-attributable age-standardised mortality; greenspace access from GLAD
PAPERS.endpoint: PM2.5-attributable ASMR; greenspace access and inequality
PAPERS.affil: Shandong University, China; Shandong University, China
PAPERS.n: 204 countries, 2000-2020. Global PM2.5-attributable all-cause ASMR fell from 63.5 to 55.4 per 100,000 while greenspace access fell from 37.0% to 28.6%; greenspace inequality in low-SDI countries rose (Gini 0.20 to 0.24). Higher greenspace access correlated with lower PM2.5-attributable mortality for IHD, stroke, COPD and neonatal disorders. Both sides are modelled country aggregates and the attributable burden is itself a function of GBD exposure and baseline rates, so the correlation is ecological and confounded by development. Mortality attributable to PM2.5 can fall while concentrations rise if baseline rates fall, so the trend is not an exposure trend. Relevance: low - burden bookkeeping with no measurement content.

PAPERS.title: Applying geographic information systems data linkages for an exposome-wide association study in the Personalized Environment and Genes Study
PAPERS.short: NIEHS PEGS GIS-ExWAS 88 geospatial exposure indicators 11 phenotypes IPTW LASSO air pollution cardiovascular
PAPERS.pm: 88 GIS-linked residential exposure indicators including air pollution
PAPERS.endpoint: 11 common disease phenotypes
PAPERS.affil: DLH LLC, USA; National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences, USA
PAPERS.n: 7,531 Personalized Environment and Genes Study participants' residential histories linked by open-source GIS to 88 exposure indicators; cross-sectional associations with 11 phenotypes by adjusted logistic regression, IPTW and LASSO. The GIS-ExWAS recovered associations complementary to the cohort's earlier questionnaire ExWAS, including air pollution with cardiovascular disease, plus new suggestive associations. No effect sizes are given; the contribution is the linkage pipeline. Cross-sectional design and many correlated indicators make every hit a hypothesis, and the abstract does not say which air-pollution surfaces were linked. Relevance: indirect - a standard linkage layer is where sensor-network surfaces would have to plug in.

PAPERS.title: Climate, Air Quality, and Emergency Department Use in Northern Germany: Protocol for a Multicenter Register Study.
PAPERS.short: Luebeck Schleswig-Holstein emergency department climate air quality infectious surveillance DLNM register protocol 2014-2024
PAPERS.pm: State environmental monitoring air-quality data linked with German Weather Service meteorology
PAPERS.endpoint: Daily ED visits overall and by disease category (planned)
PAPERS.affil: University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein, Germany; University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein, Germany
PAPERS.n: Protocol for a four-site retrospective study of emergency department presentations in the Luebeck area, January 2014-December 2024, linking ICD-coded visits to German Weather Service meteorology, state air-quality monitoring and Robert Koch Institute infectious surveillance. Distributed lag nonlinear models within GAMs, stratified by age, sex and socioeconomic status; ethics granted July 2025 and data transfer under way. No results. The analysis plan centres on temperature; the abstract names no particle metric, and a maritime region with few monitors will give little PM contrast. Relevance: low - noted as an upcoming low-concentration ED series.

PAPERS.title: Spatiotemporal distribution, source apportionment and cancer risk of PM-bound PCDD/Fs, PCBs and PCNs in three East Asian cities with contrasting emissions: Ulaanbaatar, Beijing and Taipei area.
PAPERS.short: Chi NYCU PM-bound PCDD/F PCB PCN TEQ Ulaanbaatar Beijing Taipei PMF source apportionment cancer risk dust events
PAPERS.design: Intensive field campaign, PMF source apportionment
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5-bound (Beijing, Taipei) and TSP-bound (Ulaanbaatar) PCDD/Fs, PCBs, PCNs; filter sampling
PAPERS.endpoint: TEQ concentrations, PMF sources, lifetime cancer risk
PAPERS.affil: National Cheng Kung University, Taiwan; National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Taiwan
PAPERS.n: 61 TSP samples in Ulaanbaatar, 24 in Beijing (22 PM2.5) and 26 PM2.5 in the Taipei area. PM2.5-bound PCDD/F TEQ averaged 107 fg/m3 in Beijing against 11.5 in Taipei; Ulaanbaatar TSP reached 128. Beijing cold-season PCDD/F TEQ rose 19-fold, and during dust events Beijing TSP TEQ (76.7) exceeded Ulaanbaatar's (48.9). PMF attributed PCDD/Fs to open burning and traffic (Ulaanbaatar), waste incineration and dust (Beijing) and boilers plus incineration and traffic (Taipei). PCDD/Fs drove over 98% of carcinogenic risk, which exceeded 1e-6 in Ulaanbaatar and Beijing, but non-inhalation pathways carried 65-90% of it. Sampling periods and size cuts differ by city, limiting comparison. Relevance: indirect - mass-based sensors cannot see the toxic-equivalent fraction that drives risk here.

PAPERS.title: A Meteorological Indicator for Particulate Matter Emissions: Adapting the Hot-Dry-Windy Index to Predict Feedlot Evening Dust Peaks
PAPERS.short: Peanusaha Auvermann Texas cattle feedlot evening dust peak Hot-Dry-Windy index water balance PM10 surface moisture
PAPERS.pm: Evening PM10 concentrations downwind of a cattle feedlot
PAPERS.endpoint: Variance in evening PM10 explained by an HDW-based moisture index
PAPERS.n: Partial abstract (Crossref). Feedlot evening dust peaks have been documented for decades but their meteorological drivers lack long-term study, and direct surface-moisture measurement is labour-intensive. The authors adapt the Hot-Dry-Windy index and couple it with precipitation in an empirical water-balance model to estimate pen-surface moisture from routine meteorology. Under the driest surface conditions the index explained 43% of the variance in evening PM10 (R2 0.433, r 0.658). The deposited text ends there, so the site, record length, PM10 instrument and performance under wetter conditions are unknown. Relevance: a cheap meteorological predictor of agricultural dust episodes, testable against low-cost PM10 sensors at feedlot fences.

PAPERS.title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling of PM2.5 ovarian toxicity: pulmonary particulate instillation associates with leukocyte infiltration and impaired granulosa cholesterol biosynthesis.
PAPERS.short: Shandong mouse intratracheal PM2.5 ovary single-cell RNA-seq leukocyte infiltration granulosa cholesterol biosynthesis STAT1 atresia
PAPERS.pm: Repeated pulmonary PM2.5 instillation in mice (dose not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Ovarian single-cell transcriptome, immune infiltration, follicular atresia
PAPERS.affil: Shandong Provincial Hospital, China; Shandong First Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: Mouse model of repeated pulmonary PM2.5 instillation with ovarian single-cell RNA-seq and in situ validation. Instillation expanded the ovarian immune compartment (B-lineage lymphocytes, neutrophils); resident macrophages took a C1qa-rich scavenger profile without NLRP3 activation. Immune-derived TGF-beta1 and TNF signalling raised JAK-STAT activity in somatic cells and suppressed the granulosa cholesterol-biosynthesis programme; trajectory modelling nominated STAT1 for follicular atresia, with p-STAT1 and TUNEL confirming in tissue. Dose, particle source and group sizes are not in the abstract, and bolus instillation is not inhalation. Relevance: low for sensing; extends the lung-to-ovary immune route behind epidemiological fecundity signals.

PAPERS.title: Particulate Matter Induces Apoptotic Death of Brain Vascular Endothelial Cells in Association with Oxidative Damage, DNA Damage Response, and MAPK/NF-B Signaling.
PAPERS.short: Korea University PM10 brain vascular endothelial cells apoptosis DNA damage MAPK NF-kB NAC zebrafish developmental toxicity
PAPERS.pm: PM10 (source and dose not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Endothelial viability, apoptosis markers, zebrafish brain vascular phenotype
PAPERS.affil: Korea University, South Korea; Korea University, South Korea
PAPERS.n: PM10 reduced brain vascular endothelial cell viability and raised TUNEL labelling, cleaved caspase-3 and PARP, intrinsic and death-receptor apoptotic proteins, DNA-damage-response markers, MAPK/NF-kB components and lipid and protein oxidation. N-acetylcysteine pretreatment improved survival and reduced caspase-substrate cleavage, implicating redox processes. In zebrafish, PM10 produced concentration-dependent developmental toxicity and altered brain vascular phenotypes. The authors themselves describe the causal chain as unresolved; doses, particle provenance and whether concentrations approach realistic deposition are not given in the abstract. Relevance: low - mechanism plausibility for the cerebrovascular and neurodevelopmental associations seen in cohorts.

PAPERS.title: Mechanisms of Airway Inflammatory Diseases Under Ozone Single Exposure, Coexposure, and Triple Exposure With PM2.5 and Heat: A Review.
PAPERS.short: Peking University review ozone PM2.5 heat coexposure triple exposure airway inflammation mechanisms immune-neuro-microbiota
PAPERS.pm: Ozone with PM2.5 and heat coexposure (mechanistic literature)
PAPERS.endpoint: Airway inflammatory disease mechanisms
PAPERS.affil: Peking University, China; Peking University, China
PAPERS.n: Review of mechanisms linking ozone alone, ozone with PM2.5 or heat, and all three to airway inflammation. Ozone injures epithelium oxidatively and activates NF-kB, MAPK and NLRP3; PM2.5 is framed as a chemical amplifier giving additive or synergistic oxidative burden, whereas heat acts as a biological sensitiser through TRP-mediated neuroimmune activation and microbiota-metabolism shifts. Triple exposure is argued to overwhelm compensation through higher effective dose, lower tolerance and convergent signalling, but the authors state its health effects are largely unexplored. No quantitative synthesis and no search protocol are described. Relevance: low for sensing; co-located O3, PM2.5 and temperature are what multi-pollutant low-cost nodes already log.

PAPERS.title: Asynchronous neurovascular and glial responses after particulate air pollution exposure declines.
PAPERS.short: Guilin critical review neurovascular glial recovery after particulate exposure reduction filtration diesel BBB microglia
PAPERS.pm: Particulate air pollution after exposure decline (filtration, emission control); diesel exhaust models
PAPERS.endpoint: Post-exposure course of BBB, microglial, metabolic and behavioural measures
PAPERS.affil: Guilin Medical University, China; Guilin Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: Critical review of experimental post-exposure studies and human exposure-reduction studies, separating cellular state, direct function and attribution. Early blood-brain barrier leakage after diesel exhaust is documented but later normalisation of the same function is not; some inflammatory markers attenuate after a switch to filtered air while other abnormalities persist for weeks or months. Human studies give both favourable and null cognitive outcomes after exposure reduction, without cell-specific recovery. The review argues for asynchronous responses rather than a common recovery sequence and sets criteria (repeated measurement of one task) for claiming recovery. Relevance: indirect - filtration-intervention trials need verified exposure drops, which indoor sensors provide.

PAPERS.title: Comparison of Bayesian hierarchical modelling and Random Forest algorithm for spatiotemporal prediction of PM10, PM2.5 and NO2 across Italy
PAPERS.short: Reatini Stafoggia Bayesian hierarchical vs random forest spatiotemporal PM10 PM2.5 NO2 prediction Italy
PAPERS.pm: Spatiotemporal PM10, PM2.5 and NO2 prediction surfaces
PAPERS.endpoint: Not recoverable at issue time
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: Elsevier day-0 deposit with no abstract in Crossref at issue time; no finding is asserted. The title states a head-to-head comparison of Bayesian hierarchical modelling and random forest for national spatiotemporal prediction of PM10, PM2.5 and NO2 across Italy; the author list (Reatini, Nobile, Stafoggia, Stortini) suggests the Italian national exposure-modelling programme. Relevance: direct if the comparison reports uncertainty calibration as well as cross-validated R2 - a Bayesian surface gives the per-cell prediction variance that guides where to add monitors, and random forest gives none without extra machinery. Recheck at the W46 abstract sweep.

PAPERS.title: Elemental characterization of PM10 sources in the pristine high-altitude western Himalayan region
PAPERS.short: Saurabh Sarangi elemental characterization PM10 sources pristine high-altitude western Himalaya
PAPERS.pm: PM10 elemental composition and sources
PAPERS.endpoint: Not recoverable at issue time
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: Elsevier day-0 deposit with no abstract in Crossref at issue time; no finding is asserted. The title describes elemental characterisation and source identification of PM10 at a pristine high-altitude site in the western Himalaya; geography is taken from the title. Sampling method, period, analytical technique and source-apportionment approach are unknown, so whether this is a filter-based XRF or ICP campaign cannot be told. Relevance: background-site composition fixes the dust and long-range transport baseline against which Indo-Gangetic and Himalayan foothill sensor networks are interpreted. Recheck at the W46 abstract sweep.

PAPERS.title: Impacts of agricultural reactive nitrogen emissions on the air quality in the Guanzhong Basin, China
PAPERS.short: Liu Guanzhong Basin agricultural reactive nitrogen ammonia emissions air quality impact
PAPERS.pm: Air-quality response to agricultural reactive nitrogen emissions (PM2.5 likely via ammonium nitrate; not confirmed)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not recoverable at issue time
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: Elsevier day-0 deposit with no abstract in Crossref at issue time; no finding is asserted. The title addresses the impact of agricultural reactive nitrogen emissions on air quality in the Guanzhong Basin (Xi'an region); whether PM2.5 is the endpoint is not stated in the metadata, and it is carried because agricultural ammonia is the lever on secondary ammonium nitrate in this basin. Relevance: ties to today's nitrate theme (Pearl River components, HONO reconstruction) if the abstract confirms a PM2.5 outcome; recheck at the W46 abstract sweep. Model or observation basis is unknown.

PAPERS.title: Assessing the relative reduction efficiency of different plant communities to atmospheric microplastics and PM2.5
PAPERS.short: Li Cao plant communities relative reduction efficiency atmospheric microplastics PM2.5 urban green space
PAPERS.pm: Atmospheric PM2.5 and airborne microplastics under different plant communities
PAPERS.endpoint: Not recoverable at issue time
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: Elsevier day-0 deposit with no abstract in Crossref at issue time; no finding is asserted. The title compares how different plant communities reduce atmospheric microplastics and PM2.5, presumably by paired in- and out-of-canopy measurement, but neither design, site, season nor instrument is available, and microplastic counting methods are not standardised. Relevance: vegetation-barrier claims rest on short paired campaigns where sensor inter-unit bias is the same size as the effect; worth checking how the reduction was measured, and over how many paired days, once the abstract appears.
